_national.varieties: VCP (Vino de Calidad Preferente) only from Vitis vinifera varieties on INAVI's approved list; Tannat is the signature grape.
_national.min_alcohol: VCP at least 12% abv (from the 2007 harvest; previously 10.5%); table wine ("Vino Comun") at least 10.5%.
_national.labelling: Two categories: VCP, sold only in glass bottles of up to 750 ml with "Vino de Calidad Preferente (VCP)" on the label in letters at least 6 mm high, and "Vino Comun" for everything else. Variety 85% (two varieties may be named only if they make 100%); vintage 85%. A geographical indication or region may be named only with certification of the right to use it; there is no DO system, and labels normally name departments (e.g. Canelones, Maldonado, Colonia). Labels are registered with INAVI and VCP lots must pass analytical and sensory checks.
_national.other: VCP analytical limits: volatile acidity max 0.80 g/l (as sulphuric acid), total SO2 max 200 mg/l (300 mg/l above 4 g/l sugar).
